executiveSummary.title: WHAT THE DATA SAYS
executiveSummary.narrative:
Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel appeared in at least one AI answer for 24.6% of the traveler needs we tested, showing that AI recognizes the hotel as relevant across a broad range of stays. Across every individual AI answer, however, Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel appeared 7.7% of the time. In practical terms, the hotel fits many of the searches being made, but a traveler will not consistently see Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel in the hotel options surfaced.

Leisure Travel is Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel's clearest competitive strength. The hotel appeared in 9.6% of AI answers for these searches, compared with 9.6% for the comparable hotels used in this analysis — about as often as the comparable hotels used in this analysis. Among AI answers where hotel ranking could be measured, Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel appeared in the Top 3 35.7% of the time, showing how prominently it is positioned when AI includes it.

The main opportunity is consistency: the hotel is already relevant across many traveler needs, so the next focus is understanding where it is absent from individual AI results. No comparable prior official monitoring period is available yet, so change over time is not shown.

sections.headline: Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel's primary issue is entering AI consideration at all, especially for Adventure & Experiences.
sections.keyInsight: AI Consideration is 7.7%, so the hotel appears in only a limited share of individual comparable responses. When the hotel is absent, New York Marriott Marquis repeatedly appears instead — a concentrated substitution pattern rather than a diffuse competitor list. Rank tactics have limited value until relevance improves. The binding constraint is becoming part of the answer set for the traveler needs the hotel currently misses.
sections.whyItMatters: Fine-tuning rank against individual competitors will have limited value until the hotel becomes relevant in more of the traveler needs it currently misses. Entry problems and rank problems require different management attention. If leadership optimizes competitor comparisons first, the hotel can look busy while still missing the larger answer-set gap.
sections.focusNow: Focus first on how the hotel is represented for Adventure & Experiences. Review whether the attributes, positioning, and use cases most relevant to those travelers are complete and consistently represented across priority sources. Treat competitor-rank tactics as secondary until entry improves.
sections.whatToReview: Compare evidence from scenarios where New York Marriott Marquis appears with the property information currently available for Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel. Check entry cues first — product type, occasion, and location framing — before broadening the review to secondary attributes.
